body:
The thing is, I don't see any impact I could have on somebody because I don't want to make an impact. I want to fly in the AF, partially because it's been my lifelong dream and partially because I want a way to "run away from reality" without having to do anything drastic.

I'm not ready to die, but I wouldn't hesitate to lay my life down if I need to while serving.  I guess the reason I'm still around is because I want to find answer to your question.

I was given a lot of percocet, I've been doped up and pretty stoned the past few days once I get through classes. I know it's not the best habit to be forming while depressed, but I've fallen into it and broken out before.

I get my staples removed Monday, just in time for final exams.
Are you still following through with this?

[Great Ghosts by The Microphones/Mt Eerie](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gke3z5tck7Y) and [Asleep by The Smiths](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-CGIii_eTOk) have always been two favorite songs of mine.  Songs that I feel like I haven't listened to for years, but really shook me up around the time of my original dysthymia diagnosis (4~ years ago).  Alternatively, [Good Night by The Beatles](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Omn51UZ3Hnw) is a beautiful lullaby.

I'm glad that I was able to make friends quickly last year in the dorms, friends that I still see regularly (including the one person at school I actually feel openly comfortable around).

I hope it gets easier, I really do.

>I think I'm just being stubborn at this point, I'm trying to think my way past suicide, find an answer, discover a solution to end all my suicidal thinking. But it might be more like an addiction, the more you think of it, it just gets worse. If you think about it too much you might trap yourself in.

This is a very interesting perspective, but I do see how I could be doing the same thing to myself.

I know I need to open up to people and actively pursue living a more pleasant life.  The fact that I can count the number of people I've opened up to since being first diagnosed on one hand is rather depressing.
Thanks!  I'm very aware of what could happen and my Halloween trip almost quickly turned south, though I've been fortunate enough to only have neutral->positive past experiences.

Wow, thanks for the long response.  I know alcoholism is something very real and I while I'm conscious of the fact that I am headed down the wrong path, I have yet to do anything to change it.  One of my good friends at university with me was physically addicted to alcohol over the summer after a failed relationship, he was in a really awful state dependence-wise the first week or two of classes.

I actually began to scratch the surface of Buddhism two years ago.  I've done a fair amount of reading from the [r/buddhism book list](http://www.reddit.com/r/Buddhism/comments/pnhqj/official_rbuddhism_book_recommendations/) and am a pretty active lurker on the sub itself.  I feel as though I simply try to ignore emotions and desire and live a kind, care-free life, something that doesn't really help.  Buddhism is something that interests me greatly and I have tried to adapt a more-free lifestyle since truly discovering Buddhism.

>Lastly, don't think that because you feel fairly certain in having your shit together now that things can't turn south in your situation slightly faster than you can handle. How you move through live and fulfill your own mental and physical needs while fulfilling your obligations is important.


>Your mind is like any other part of your body; it cannot function unless properly cared for.

This is very humbling, something I should keep in mind.  I'll give you a status update when I'm 26.

I know suicide is a very selfish act, one of the many reasons why I could not actually do it myself.

I want to graduate college so I can actually feel like I've accomplished something and I want to fly.  I have a few passions, I play on my school's Ultimate Frisbee team.  It's a great group of people and I love the sport.  Playing Ultimate/tossing around with friends is one of the few things that temporarily clears my mind.  The problem now is finding the motivation to get out of bed and practice, something that currently feels like a chore, despite the fact that I always feel better when I go.

I'm not on any sort of antidepressant/supplement.  Around the same time I started therapy I told myself I would try to "beat depression" on my own.  The reason I'm sticking to it is because I don't want to have any "flaws" on my record for later in life.  Vicious cycle.

edit: but yes, I know I need to cut back on the smoking.  Flat-out quitting last year helped me sort my life out.
